text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Friday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Parliament supported the new government of Andris Shkele by 70 votes in favour and 17 against. The number of minister has been reduced to 18 against 29. There are four ministers of state in charge of reforms in state revenues, local governments, health care and environment protection. A new finance minister, which caused the downfall of the previous government, was not chosen.

- Unemployment in Latvia was 7.3 percent in January, an increase of 0.1 percent on December. A year ago the level of unemployment was 6.5 percent. The worst hit region is eastern Latgale, where unemployment runs at over 20 percent.
- Talks on land border demarcation between Latvia and Russia are due to resume in Moscow on February 24.
- Energy supply regulatory body is to decide an a possible rise in electricity tariffs today.
- The deadline for signing a stock purchase agreement with German Preussen Electra and Ruhrgas, strategic investors in Latvian Gas, was extended until April 1.
